developer: Forus Technology, Inc. (formerly Tandem). Founder & CEO: Sahir Jaggi. Clinical Intelligence led by Adam Harris, MD (former VP of Applied AI at Oscar Health; Clinical Assistant Professor, NYU School of Medicine) and Kathleen Alvarez, NP (Yale School of Nursing).
availability: Available in the United States. Accessible via website for providers (forus.com). Supports providers across all 50 states. Not known to be available outside the U.S.
summary: Forus is an AI-powered platform that automates the end-to-end medication access process, including prior authorization (PA) submission, appeals, pharmacy routing, affordability/enrollment in patient assistance programs, and patient communication.
medicalPurpose: Intended for physician practices and their staff to automate all steps of obtaining prior authorization, from prescribing the medication to the patient actually getting it. This includes PA form generation and submission, appeals, enrollment forms, benefit verifications, PA renewal tracking, and patient communication.
acceptableInput: Electronic prescriptions (structured data) or manual upload of patient records.
output: Completed prior authorization forms, appeal letters, enrollment forms, patient communication, pharmacy routing information. How output is generated: 1. Patient records and prescription data are pulled from the EHR (via integration) or uploaded directly to Forus. 2. AI auto-generates PA form content within the same day and submits. 3. Forus conducts follow-ups. 4. If denied, Forus generates an appeal letter for provider review and submits. 5. Forus routes the prescription to the correct pharmacy.
roleInDecisionMaking: The platform automates administrative work and does not make clinical decisions.
intendedUsers: Doctors and their staff, including providers of all sizes from 1-2 provider private practices to large physician groups and health systems. Provider must be able to e-prescribe (electronic prescriptions only; Forus does not currently support non-eRx practices).
targetPatientPopulation: All U.S. patients who are prescribed medications requiring prior authorization. Forus supports every medication, insurance, and pharmacy, including both retail and specialty drugs.
knownPerformanceLimitations: Based on publicly available third-party reviews and developer materials: Forus is designed for medication prior authorizations and may have limited capability for non-medication PA categories (e.g., procedures, imaging, DME). Performance may vary for complex or unusual cases with 'snags from insurance' or when patients do not respond to Forus's outreach prompts. Requires patient engagement (patients must interact with SMS prompts for certain steps). Not a complete replacement for dedicated PA specialists in complex, high-volume, or multi-category authorization environments. Requires EHR e-prescribing capability; does not support fax or phone-based prescribing workflows. Specific AI model limitations and error rates are not publicly disclosed.
skinTypeRepresentationEquity: Not formally measured or disclosed. Forus's platform is administrative in nature, so skin tone representation is not directly applicable to its core PA automation function. The platform's design goal of supporting 'every drug, insurance, and pharmacy' implies an intention to provide equitable access across patient populations regardless of insurance type, drug cost, or specialty. The platform includes affordability features — identifying financial assistance programs — intended to improve access for patients who may face cost barriers.
requiredClinicianOversight: Yes. All of Forus's work is administrative and workflow automation, starting after the clinician submits a prescription. Forus automates administrative workflow steps after the prescription is placed to help make sure the patient gets the medication.
modelType: AI-powered workflow automation platform using a human-in-the-loop approach, combining natural language processing (NLP) for reading clinical records and generating PA forms and appeal letters, machine learning for predicting PA approval likelihood, identifying optimal appeal strategies, and recognizing payer-specific patterns from historical data. Includes rules-based automation for payer-specific PA form completion and formulary/policy matching. The platform learns from each processed case, with the Clinical Intelligence team (led by Adam Harris, MD) embedded in product design and QA.

trainingData.description: Not publicly disclosed. The platform — Forus, previously called Tandem — has machine learning models trained on proprietary datasets of prior authorization interactions collected through the platform (described as 'first-party data' and 'millions of prior authorization interactions'). The developer does not publicly specify which large language models or foundation models underlie the NLP capabilities. Forus's specific foundation models are not confirmed publicly.

modelDevelopmentAndValidation.description: No external or independent validation process is publicly disclosed. The platform's engineering blog describes how Forus employs LLM-as-judge evaluator systems for quality monitoring. Case studies from individual practices are available on the Forus blog, including how Goodman Dermatology helps patients access medications after denials.

clinicalTrial.description: None identified. No peer-reviewed publications found.

performance.summary: Traditional model performance metrics are not available; however performance metrics from individual case studies can be found on Forus's website. From Forus's case studies on its blog: at one practice called Family Allergy and Asthma, Forus cut PA turnaround time from 7+ days to 1.1 and reduced per-patient workload by 70%. At another, called DOCS Dermatology, they helped achieve same-day submission and approvals in <1 day.
